fidelity_rungs.role: cheapest rung on the frozen verification ladder; converges and validates like any other, and is wrong by 3.3% on the QoI
the finest rung of the frozen ladder — the one that earned ANALYTICALLY_VERIFIED at 3.97e-04 relative error

held_constant_across_rungs: slab length, end time, boundary and initial conditions
non_goals: no adaptive fidelity selection — nothing here chooses a rung
no campaign, no EVPI, no EVSI, no certification, no model adequacy
no physical validation; the hidden truth is synthetic and known
no new inference framework beyond a grid posterior over one parameter

observation_model.note: noise is injected by the benchmark; the solver is deterministic and no measurement of anything physical occurs

prediction_before_execution.basis: alpha_bias = discretization_error / |du/dalpha|, with the discretization errors taken from the frozen thermal verification gate at alpha = 1.2e-5. This is a prediction to be checked, not a threshold to be met: T1 has no pass/fail gate and therefore nothing to tune

config.scientific_question: Can a numerically coarse but apparently converged solver produce a posterior over alpha that is confident yet systematically biased?

truth.scope: synthetic hidden truth with a known alpha; no physical validation and no real measurement is involved
truth.truth_source: exact analytic solution + declared Gaussian noise
